clue.text: Trout producer to rest uneasily, having eaten carp

indicators.note: having eaten means the reshuffled letters swallow the fish, taking it inside
resting uneasily means the four letters of rest toss and turn into a new order

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone tries to rest but cannot settle after a heavy meal of carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trout' is not a fish here but the Trout Quintet, so its producer is the composer; 'uneasily' scrambles rest to SERT before 'having eaten' takes in the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote the Trout Quintet, so he is the work's creator.

clue.text: Quest to burn church

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or burn

explanation.surface: A zealous mission to set fire to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a hunt or seeking out of something.

clue.text: Offering an unattractive bouquet, being unsentimental?

definitions.meaning: read literally, having a harsh nose, as a wine taster says of an unpleasant aroma
tough-minded and practical, without soft feelings

explanation.surface: A wine with a nasty smell is described as tough and practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' is a wine's aroma, its 'nose'; a wine whose nose is harsh is literally hard-nosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine with a harsh smell has a rough nose; a businesslike, tough person is called hard-nosed.

clue.text: Flirtation with model "babe" results in famous engagement

indicators.note: the flirtation, model and babe combine and what they result in is a rearrangement of their letters

parts.note: the Model T was the famous early Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A flirtation with a glamour model ends up in a celebrated engagement, as in a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests a wedding but means a battle. 'results in' rearranges FLIRTATION, T and BABE into the 1940 air battle over southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1940 air campaign between the RAF and the Luftwaffe is one of history's best-known battles.

clue.text: It's awarded for covering animal's home with eggs

indicators.note: covering means the eggs go round the outside of the den

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: A prize is handed out for protecting an animal's den with eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is a badger, whose burrow is called a sett; 'covering' wraps the eggs around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is the ribbon badge given to winners at shows.

clue.text: Big Welshwoman, not a real poet

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for big people
Sian is a common Welsh woman's name

explanation.surface: A large woman from Wales is no genuine poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The poems of this Gaelic bard were produced by James Macpherson in the 1760s, so the poet himself never existed as presented.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed ancient Gaelic bard was a literary invention of James Macpherson.

clue.text: The striking of hands on feet

definitions.text: The striking of hands on feet

parts.words: The striking of hands on feet
parts.note: an audience clapping its hands while up on its feet: a tribute where everyone rises to applaud

explanation.walkthrough: 'striking of hands' sounds like a fight or a craft, but it is clapping; 'on feet' means standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping while risen from one's seat is the highest form of theatre applause.

clue.text: Not much land has been rented

parts.note: in 'is let', is serves as the auxiliary for 'has been'
let means hired out or rented

explanation.surface: A small plot has already been leased out.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a tiny island, only a small piece of ground.

clue.text: Votes against accepting round sum of money at present

indicators.note: accepting means the votes take the other pieces inside them

parts.note: nays are votes against a motion
O is round in shape
a wad is a bundle or sum of money

explanation.surface: Opposing votes are cast when someone accepts a bribe, a sum of money, at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the current era, these days.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about a student's footwear

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the other letters

parts.note: gosh is an exclamation of surprise
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a student's shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a rubber overshoe worn in wet weather.

clue.text: One afraid of the devil

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a man'
frit is British dialect for frightened

explanation.surface: Someone is scared of the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIT is a Northern English dialect word for frightened. 'One afraid of the devil' reads as a nervous person, but the devil is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful evil spirit or demon in Arabic mythology.

clue.text: Do better than a female in sluggish strait

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the word for sluggish

parts.note: slow means sluggish
to cap is to outdo or better

explanation.surface: A woman is outdone in a slow-moving channel of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a British naval anchorage, the sheltered water among the Orkney islands; 'in' puts the outdoing, a and female inside sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orkney anchorage is a stretch of sea enclosed by islands, a sound or channel.

clue.text: Is a Balt permitted to love a painter?

parts.note: 'Is ... permitted' asks 'can', the clue's question form
a Lett is a Latvian, one of the Baltic peoples
love is nil in tennis, giving O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Latvian may fall in love with an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is ... permitted' becomes CAN; read 'can a Lett O', with O for love, the tennis score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian artist is famous for his detailed views of Venice and London.

clue.text: Took out for being pass

definitions.meaning: took out means escorted on a romantic outing

explanation.surface: Someone was taken out on a date because they were old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The page drops the accent: 'pass' is passé, out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Escorting someone on a romantic outing is going on a date; something old-fashioned is behind the times.

clue.text: Tree with mineral source on the land

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
ore is rock from which metals and minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: A tree grows beside a mineral deposit on dry ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on the shore or on land rather than at sea.

clue.text: Good person tucked into spread with rectitude

indicators.note: tucked into means the good person goes inside the spread

parts.note: honey is a sweet spread for bread
ST, saint, is the crossword good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous person eats a spread with righteous manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it signals placing the saint inside the spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectitude is moral uprightness, truthfulness and integrity.

clue.text: Likely candidates are not tall and lean

parts.note: short means not tall
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: The plausible applicants are short and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like thin but is the verb: a ship that leans lists.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final selection of applicants considered for a post.

clue.text: Degree and unit of purity in game

parts.note: bac, short for baccalaureate, is an academic qualification
a carat measures the purity of gold

explanation.surface: A degree and a gold-purity unit are found in some game.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game popular in casinos.

clue.text: Making some noise, having fit about historic declaration

indicators.note: about means the word for fit goes round the declaration

parts.note: able means fit or capable
UDI was Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence of 1965

explanation.surface: Someone having a fit shouts about a historic statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a seizure but means capable, ABLE. UDI was Rhodesia's 1965 Unilateral Declaration of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be heard is producing sound loud enough to reach the ear.

clue.text: Detection of one in sin getting upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, read bottom to top
in means the one goes inside the word for sin

parts.note: a lapse is a moral slip or sin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a sinner and becomes distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LAPSE to give LAPISE; 'getting upset' turns it upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is the act of spying or noticing something.

clue.text: Backing and not backing particle

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: the second backing means the word not is written backwards

parts.note: the word not as written

explanation.surface: Someone both supports and does not support a particle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' does two jobs in two places: first as support, PRO, then as reversal of NOT to TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a positively charged subatomic particle in the atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Leader — that of Roman Empire, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of Empire with R could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Roman, as in type style

explanation.surface: The chief figure is the one at the head of the Roman Empire, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges R and EMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister is the country's head of government, its chief.

clue.text: Little-known composer interrupted by accountant

indicators.note: interrupted by means the accountant is put into the middle of the composer

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An obscure composer is cut off by a bookkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer is Thomas Arne, 18th-century English author of Rule, Britannia!; 'interrupted by' breaks him open for the accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious or understood by few people.

clue.text: Island where there's a lot of piracy about

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An island notorious for widespread piracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims piracy to PIRAC, and 'about' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian holiday isle lies in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Irritating person adding nothing to the sauce

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An annoying person contributes nothing to the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adding nothing' sounds like contributing nothing, but adds the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil and pine-nut paste for pasta.

clue.text: Hack provides publicity involving terrorists

indicators.note: involving means the publicity piece takes the terrorists inside it

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement, publicity
ETA was the Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: A journalist produces advertising about a terrorist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist but here means a bad poet. ETA was a Basque separatist group in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster writes trashy, inferior verse: a literary drudge.

clue.text: Emperor or king from a distant place in the drink

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin king

indicators.note: in means the distance word goes inside the wine

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
afar means from far away

explanation.surface: An emperor or a king traveled from far away to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Haile Selassie was known by this name and title before becoming Emperor of Ethiopia; 'in' puts the distance word inside the Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title and name of Haile Selassie before he became Ethiopia's ruler.

clue.text: Some Nazi bigots returning to the island

indicators.note: returning means that stretch is read backwards
some means only part of the words is used, a stretch within them

explanation.surface: A group of Nazi bigots comes back to the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'nAZI BIgots' is AZIBI; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balearic isle is in the Mediterranean, famous for nightclubs.

clue.text: Being aroused by a type of shirt is problematic

parts.note: a T-shirt is a type of shirt, giving T
horny is slang for sexually aroused

explanation.surface: Being excited by a certain shirt is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny issue is difficult and controversial, like a prickly plant.

clue.text: Dark savage circumventing trap

indicators.note: circumventing means going around, so the savage surrounds the trap

parts.note: a brute is a savage person
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A dark savage gets round a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' as a noun names a dark-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark brown hair, so the word describes darkness of colouring.
